scenes.title: Ecobee humidity reading wrong
scenes.body: Vienna, VA

scenes.title: Ecobee says 63%. The meter says 50%.
scenes.body: A 13-point humidity gap, with spikes to 70%. Normal sensor error is about ±5%.

scenes.title: New ecobee on a Carrier heat pump
scenes.body: Here's how we found the cause and fixed it, in 6 steps.

scenes.title: Test it properly
scenes.body: Tape the meter right beside the thermostat. Fan on Auto, minimum runtime 0. Wait 30–60 min.

scenes.title: Seal the hole behind the thermostat
scenes.body: Power off. Pack duct seal around the wires so wall-cavity air can't hit the sensor.

scenes.title: Seal the other end
scenes.body: Seal where the thermostat cable enters the air handler. The blower pulls air down the wall.

scenes.title: Verify the wiring
scenes.body: Old thermostat, ecobee and air handler must match. Tug-test every wire.

scenes.title: Check the setup
scenes.body: Heat pump type, O/B on cool (Carrier), fan controlled by the thermostat.

scenes.title: Correct what's left
scenes.body: Only after sealing: enter the steady gap in Humidity Correction (e.g. 60% vs 50% → −10%).

scenes.title: 52% — matching the meter
scenes.body: Air quality went from Poor to Clean. Most "bad sensor" calls are air leaks.
